RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Riley Jennings
Member ID: W995720068
Reference number: POC-39DE00339B-16726
Date of notice: 2026-08-19
Requested service: Knee arthroscopy / meniscus surgery, CPT 29881
Treating surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

To the Appeals Review Committee:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881 (knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy), dated 2026-08-19, reference number POC-39DE00339B-16726. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity."

I want to be direct about what I am and am not able to cite in this letter. UPMC Health Plan's public provider materials state that the plan uses licensed InterQual® criteria to make medical necessity determinations for prior authorization, and that the specific criteria set referenced internally (described on the plan's own Policies & Procedures Manual page as "CRM.003") is not published for public or member review; the plan directs members and providers to contact Member Services or Provider Services for those details. I have not been given the text of the specific criteria applied to this request, and I am not able to quote plan policy language I have not seen. I am not attributing any quoted language to UPMC Health Plan in this letter. Instead, I am submitting the complete clinical record below and formally requesting, as part of this appeal, that UPMC Health Plan identify in writing exactly which specific criteria (by policy/criteria-set name, number, and section) were not met, and which specific documentation was considered missing, so that I and my surgeon can respond precisely if further information is needed.

Below is a summary of the clinical documentation that was submitted (or is available to submit) in support of medical necessity for this procedure. I believe this information directly addresses the stated basis for denial — that the documentation was "incomplete."

1. Symptom duration and course: I have had 9 months of progressive knee pain that has not been relieved by rest.

2. Conservative treatment already completed:
   - Supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, completed over 10 weeks (2026-05-08 to 2026-07-17), with 16 visits documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
   - NSAID therapy for 4 months, with inadequate relief.
   - A corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-13, which provided only 2 weeks of partial relief.

3. Objective imaging findings: MRI of the knee performed 2026-07-18 shows a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking. Articular cartilage is preserved, and the knee is Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 (i.e., minimal degenerative change), which is clinically relevant because it indicates this is a mechanical meniscal problem rather than advanced osteoarthritis.

4. Functional limitation: I experience locking and giving way of the knee, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking only.

5. Physical examination findings: Positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

6. Absence of contraindications: There is no active infection and no untreated substance use disorder. My BMI is 29. I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, this record documents a symptomatic, imaging-confirmed displaced meniscal tear with mechanical locking, a functional impairment affecting daily activity, and a completed, adequately dosed trial of conservative management (supervised physical therapy, prolonged NSAID use, and a corticosteroid injection) that has failed to relieve symptoms. If any specific element of this record — a particular note, a specific measurement, a specific date range, or a specific provider attestation — was missing from what was actually submitted with the prior authorization request, I am requesting that UPMC Health Plan specify exactly what is missing so my surgeon's office, Dr. Lindqvist, can supply it immediately. All of the underlying source documents referenced above (physical therapy discharge note, injection procedure note, MRI report dated 2026-07-18, and the surgeon's clinic notes documenting exam findings and functional limitations) are available and are being submitted with this appeal as attachments.

I am also requesting, in connection with this appeal:
- A copy of the specific medical necessity criteria (InterQual criteria set or other policy) that was applied to this request, including the policy/criteria-set name, number, and effective date;
- Written confirmation of which specific piece(s) of documentation were considered incomplete or missing at the time of the initial review; and
- The opportunity for Dr. Lindqvist to participate in a peer-to-peer discussion with a UPMC medical director regarding this determination, as described in UPMC Health Plan's provider materials.

I understand that this appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, i.e., by 2027-02-15, and I am submitting this letter well within that deadline.

Please contact me at [phone number] or [email address] if any additional information is needed to complete this appeal. I have also asked Dr. Lindqvist's office to send any additional records directly to your office if that is more efficient, and their office contact information is [surgeon's office phone/fax].

Thank you for your prompt reconsideration of this determination.

Sincerely,

Riley Jennings
Member ID: W995720068

- Corticosteroid injection procedure note (2026-06-13)
